newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares close mixed despite IMF hopes.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares close mixed despite IMF hopes.

text.p: Leading Russian shares closed mixed on Tuesday despite renewed hopes the International Monetary Fund would pay out delayed loan tranches, dealers said.
They said news that an IMF mission had recommended that the Fund board should meet on Friday on whether to pay out the delayed loan tranches, made no impact on the market.
"When the IMF pays us the tranche, an extra couple of million will come, not earlier," said Andrei Kukk, chief trader at Rinaco-Plus.

Kukk said Surgutneftegaz had risen for two hours on the news that Surgut management had agreed to take steps to put right violations of securities law which arose as a result of last October's share issue.
"The rise lasted while there were orders, which were quickly fulfilled," he said.
Surgutneftegz rose to $0.420 from $0.405 at Monday's close and Surgutneftegaz preferred rose to $0.29 from $0.276.
Kukk said the passage of the 1997 draft budget, due to be discussed by the State Duma lower house of parliament on Sunday, would have little impact on share prices.
"The quicker it is passed the quicker the money will come, but it will not be a buy signal," Kukk said.
Nizhnevartovskneftegaz was the main loser of the day with the share plummeting to $5.00 from $8.10 after a sharp rise on Monday, said Andrei Ippolitov, corporate securities director at IK Prospekt.
Traders forecast a lethargic market until the end of New Year and orthodox Christmas holidays.

Sinarsky Trubny Zavod rose to $1.6 from $1.5 on December 6 close when it was last traded, Gazprom was $0.320 after $0.309, Rostelekom rose to $2.34 from $2.29, Mosenergo edged up to $0.973 from $0.970 and Novosibirskenergo fell to $2.8 from $3.0.
